citationText: K. Kitamura, T. Yasue, T. Soeno, and H. Shimamoto, “Full-Specification 8K Camera System,” Proc. 2017 NAB BEC, pp. 266–271, Apr. 2016. Conclusion We have upgraded our 8K 240-frames/sec camera system by adding three new modes: 480-frames/sec shooting, 120-frames/sec random noise reduction shooting, and 120-frames/sec flicker reduction shooting. In the 480-frames/sec shooting mode, we captured 8K 480-frames/sec images without visible lag by operating the image sensor at double the normal speed. However, the SNR of 480-frames/sec images was degraded more than expected. Therefore, it is necessary to improve image sensor operation in the 480-frames/sec mode to obtain a reasonable image quality. We also confirmed the effectiveness of random noise reduction and flicker reduction in the 120-frames/ sec shooting mode. These image quality improvement functions can be applied to various video cameras and will be introduced in future 8K cameras as required functions. We will continue to improve the image quality of the 480-frames/sec images and utilize the camera system for various 8K content productions by using the newly added functions. (a) Current 120-fps shooting Time [Frame at 120-fps] 0.97 0.98 0.99
